record.paper_title: String Theory on ADS3: Some Open Questions
record.context_brief: physical representations and vertex operators in the string spectrum
record.original_question: For string theory on the SU(1,1) group manifold, after coupling the SU(1,1) Wess–Zumino–Witten model to two-dimensional gravity and imposing Virasoro constraints, which left- and right-moving SU(1,1)L × SU(1,1)R current-algebra representations should be kept so that the string theory has a well-behaved operator algebra, positive-norm physical states, a clear role for discrete and continuous representations, and identifiable particle states with corresponding vertex operators?

evidence.quote: The coupling of the above conformal model to the two-dimensional gravity creates spurious states that we should eliminate from the spectrum.

In this analysis, the natural questions are the following: What are the representations of the SU(1,1)L × SU(1,1)R current algebra that should be kept in order to have a consistent theory (in particular a well-behaved operator algebra)? What are the roles of discrete versus continuous representations? Are all physical states of positive norm? What kind of particles do these states describe, and what are the corresponding vertex operators?
there is no satisfactory selection of representations that can be performed, which guarantees the absence of negative-norm states in the physical Hilbert space.

artifact.category_tag: SL(2,R) WZW model and strings on AdS3
artifact.status_search_result: The question was essentially resolved by Maldacena and Ooguri (hep-th/0001053, J. Math. Phys. 42 (2001) 2929), who proposed the spectrum of the SL(2,ℝ) WZW model as continuous representations with j = 1/2 + is and discrete representations with 1/2 < j < (k-1)/2, together with all their spectral-flow images (parameterized by an integer winding number w), and proved a no-ghost theorem for these representations. Continuous representations correspond to long strings and discrete ones to short strings; vertex operators were constructed explicitly. Companion papers (Part 2, hep-th/0005183; Part 3, hep-th/0111180) extended the analysis to the partition function and correlation functions, confirming consistency.

status_evidence.title: Strings in AdS_3 and the SL(2,R) WZW Model. Part 1: The Spectrum
status_evidence.snippet: We study the spectrum of bosonic string theory on AdS_3... We prove a no ghost theorem for all the representations that are involved... new representations obtained by spectral flow.
status_evidence.claim: Maldacena–Ooguri identified the allowed SL(2,R) representations (continuous and discrete series plus spectral flow) and proved a no-ghost theorem, addressing the selection question.

status_evidence.title: Strings in AdS(3) and the SL(2,R) WZW model. Part 3: Correlation Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Correlation functions for string theory on AdS_3 are computed consistently with the proposed spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: The operator algebra was shown to be consistent with the proposed spectrum, confirming the resolution.
